newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo issues warning on Lamictal.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo issues warning on Lamictal.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Thursday it was issuing a warning to physicians about the side effects of its epilepsy drug Lamictal.
The British pharmaceutical giant said new data suggest the incidence of serious skin rashes in children was between one in 100 and one in 300, significantly higher than in adults.
"The incidence of skin reactions was already documented, and in adults was one in 1,000. Our data suggests it's higher in children," a spokeswoman for the company said.

Glaxo said it was in the process of sending letters to doctors who prescribe the drug, which helps control epileptic seizures. The first warnings were issued to U.S. physicians on Wednesday, the company said. Letters were being sent to UK doctors on Thursday.
Lamictal was first available in Ireland in 1991. Since then, it was approved in 72 countries and is used by some 800,000 patients worldwide.
At the end of 1996, Lamictal sales were 105 million stg, about 1.25 percent of the company's total revenue. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
